summary: Pickett Peak Lookout, Trinity County: lookout site since 1922, tower collapsed 1933, current cab on 1965 tower, reopened with paid staff 2013; not in regular use per 2023 sources.

facts.design: National Plan CL-100 13x13 cabin on a 55-foot K-Brace steel tower, built 1965 per NHLR

staffing.status: not staffed regularly per an undated Peakbagging page; a 2023 hiking blog says no longer in use

visit.trail_note: A 2023 account reached the lookout on foot from the Bailey Canyon Campground trailhead. Road maps disagree: an older map shows pavement to the Pickett Peak Campground, newer maps show high clearance. The sources read give no official access rule; do not climb the tower.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service: Shasta-Trinity National Forest per NHLR; Peakbagging places it on the Six Rivers and Trinity boundary

events.note: NHLR says the site has served as a lookout since at least 1922

Lookout noticed a fire that seemed to be spreading; a fireman sent to investigate found it nearing the Forest boundary and went to work on it (district news item dated October 13, 1922; the fire was in September)
A 60-foot steel tower collapsed in a winter snow storm; a newspaper said it would probably be an almost total loss
Current structure: National Plan CL-100 13x13 cabin on a 55-foot K-Brace steel tower, built 1965 per NHLR
Tower footing with a date of 1972; Peakbagging says the tower was probably built then, which conflicts with the NHLR 1965 date
Reopened with paid U.S. Forest Service staffing after 20 years shuttered; lightning fires spotted and reported from it in August
Registered October 30, 2019 as NHLR US 1369, CA 192
Hiking blog says the lookout is no longer in use but still solid enough to visit; not an official status

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register places the lookout in the Shasta-Trinity National Forest; Peakbagging places it on the boundary of the Six Rivers and Trinity forests; the 2013 report says southwest of Hayfork. The story reports the disagreement.
The Register gives 5,183 feet (1,580 m); Peakbagging gives 5,778 feet. The story gives the Register figure and reports Peakbagging's.
The Register dates the current structure to 1965; Peakbagging reports a footing dated 1972 and says the tower was probably built then. The story reports both and does not choose.

corrections.why: 18.3 m is about 60 feet, the height of the tower reported collapsed in 1933. The Register gives the current 1965 tower as 55 feet.

notes_for_editor: Today's status is the weakest part: the only 2023 source is a hiking blog, which describes climbing the tower; the story does not encourage that, and the record should not treat the blog as an official status. No official access rule or closure notice was found. Peakbagging's staffing line is undated. Build-date conflict (1965 Register vs 1972 footing) is reported, not resolved. A 2018 Trinity Journal snippet says the lookout dates to 1972; that article returned HTTP 429 to fetch_text and was not read or cited. The Forest Service project summary for fire-detection cameras on Shasta-Trinity (search snippet only) was not read and may or may not involve this site. Photos: the NHLR page has a photo credit (2009, courtesy of Ron Kemnow; 1972 anchor pier, courtesy of peakbagging.com) but no image URLs were read, so none added. Budget: 6 distinct pages read (NHLR, Weebly, 2013 FFLA report, Peakbagging, valhikes blog, FS trail page) against 6, plus 2 web searches. The brief's 1965 build and 2013 staffing events are confirmed; the brief's 2019 registration is confirmed.
